workingTitle: JWST finds glassy ice in a young planetary system
publicationStatus: Peer-reviewed research article published in Science on November 12, 2026
coreFacts: JWST NIRSpec mapped reflected light from the edge-on debris disk around Beta Pictoris across 0.6 to 5.2 micrometres.
Spectra extracted from two regions about 100 astronomical units from the star show water-ice absorption near 3 micrometres and carbon-dioxide ice features near 4.26 and 4.39 micrometres.
The inferred carbon-dioxide to water-ice column-density ratio is about 1 to 9.3, or roughly 11 percent.
The water ice is predominantly amorphous, with crystalline ice contributing less than 7 percent of the ice volume at a three-sigma upper limit.
The similar ice signatures on both sides of the disk and their broad distribution are more consistent with many small collisions among volatile-rich bodies than one recent large collision.
The cold, amorphous mixture may preserve material formed in a molecular cloud or an early protostellar envelope, but that origin is inferred rather than directly dated.
sourceStatus: Full author manuscript, journal metadata, methods, measured band profiles, abundance estimates, ice-structure modeling, and collision interpretation read; measured signatures and inferred origins checked separately.
caveats: The observations identify spectral features in scattered light rather than resolving individual icy planetesimals.
The carbon-dioxide and water mixing geometry is inferred by comparison with laboratory spectra; other mixtures cannot be fully excluded.
The amorphous ice fraction is model-dependent, although crystalline ice is constrained to less than 7 percent of the ice volume.
Frequent small collisions and an interstellar or protostellar origin are interpretations of the uniform distribution and composition, not direct observations of the formation history.
